title: Applied ML evals: integrated onboarding, quantization profiles, and regression triage playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's applied ML evaluation practices: the eval harness, prompt sets and benchmarks, model onboarding checklist, quality guardrails, quantization profile guidance, and a regression triage runbook. It is intended for ML engineers, applied ML researchers, and SRE owners who operate model serving and continuous evaluation pipelines.

Goals:
- Ensure new models meet quality and latency requirements before serving to production routes.
- Provide reproducible evals and benchmark artifacts for onboarding and regressions.
- Standardize quantization profiles to balance cost and quality across hardware.
- Define a clear triage and rollback process for regressions.

Scope:
- Applies to all models entering Redwood's model catalog (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Covers text generation, chat flows, embeddings, and reranking tasks.
- Excludes proprietary customer prompt and data handling guidance (see security team pages).

Principles:
1. Automate where possible: every onboarding must run through CI-connected eval harness.
2. Fail fast and observable: regressions should be detected by lightweight monitors before user impact.
3. Reproducibility: every benchmark includes a seed, model version, config, and prompt set.
4. Conservative quantization: prefer per-workload profiles with explicit quality targets.

1) Eval harness (standards and expectations)
- Purpose: provide a reproducible, CI-friendly framework for running unit/regression and integration evals across models and hardware.
- Components:
  - Runner: executes prompt sets against a model variant with configurable parallelism and KV cache state.
  - Metrics collector: token-level latencies, throughput, perplexity, BLEU/ROUGE where appropriate, and custom task metrics.
  - Comparator: diff tool for output distributions, embedding drift, and output-classification regressions.
  - Artifact storage: store raw outputs, metrics JSON, and reproducible environment metadata.

Minimum eval harness config (example table):
| field | description | example |
| model_variant | model id + revision | redwood/open-7b:v1 |
| prompt_set_id | canonical prompts for task | ps_chat_summarization_v2 |
| seed | RNG seed for deterministic behaviors | 42 |
| max_tokens | max generation length | 512 |
| temperature | sampling temperature | 0.0 (deterministic) |
| hardware_target | cpu/cuda/tpu | gpu-a100-40gb |

CLI example (run locally / CI):
```
ri-eval-run --model redwood/open-7b:v1 --prompt-set ps_chat_summarization_v2 --out artifacts/run-2028-11-15 --runs 100 --seed 42
```

2) Prompt sets & benchmarks (guidelines)
- Prompt set construction:
  - Use representative inputs from product telemetry (anonymized) where available.
  - Include edge cases: long inputs, ambiguous phrasing, adversarial examples, and domain-specific jargon.
  - Label expected outputs where possible (reference answers, classification labels, embeddings similarity thresholds).
- Benchmark naming: <task>-<domain>-v# (e.g., summarization-support-v2).
- Required metadata per prompt set (stored in prompt_set.yaml):
  - author, created_at, task, domain, distribution notes, sample_size, anonymization notes, intended baselines.

3) Model onboarding guide (step-by-step)
1. Create model entry in catalog (model id, architecture, revision, exec constraints).
2. Attach baseline prompt sets (smoke + full).
3. Run unit-level evals (100 samples) with deterministic config (temperature=0.0).
4. Run full benchmarks (n>=500 where feasible) across representative hardware profiles.
5. Quantization profile test: run int8/quantized variants against same prompts and compare metrics.
6. Review results with reviewers and document acceptance criteria.
7. Promote to canary route with traffic cap (default 5%) and elevated monitoring for 48-72 hours.
8. Full rollout if canary meets SLOs and no regression alerts.

Onboarding checklist (short):
- [ ] Model catalog entry created
- [ ] Prompt sets assigned
- [ ] Eval harness runs completed (unit + full)
- [ ] Quantization tests executed
- [ ] Reviewer sign-off recorded
- [ ] Canary rollout scheduled

Ownership: model owner (ML eng) is primary; platform (eng-platform) supports routing and canary. Security reviews required for private deployments.

4) Quality guardrails
- Guardrail categories:
  - Functional correctness: task-specific metric drop (e.g., exact match, F1) > 5% relative to baseline triggers investigation.
  - Semantic drift: embedding cosine similarity mean shift > 0.08 for retrieval tasks triggers triage.
  - Toxicity/regulatory: any toxic classification rate above historical max triggers immediate hold.
  - Latency: P95 token-latency increase > 20% vs baseline triggers scaling or rollback policies.
- Automated detectors:
  - Canary monitors: run a 50-sample smoke set per 15m from each route.
  - Continuous evals: nightly full-run against core prompt sets, results stored in artifacts and compared to baseline.

5) Quantization profiles (recommendations and table)
- Purpose: reduce cost by lowering compute while preserving quality.
- Profiles are per-model-per-workload and must include an acceptance threshold.

Quantization profile table (example):
| profile_name | quant_scheme | hardware | acceptable_quality_drop | recommended_tasks |
| conservative-int8 | q8_clean | A100/H100 | <= 1.5% exact-match drop | classification, short generation |
| balanced-int8 | q8_mixed | A100 40GB | <= 3% quality drop | chat, summarization |
| aggressive-4bit | q4_advanced | T4 / L4 | <= 6% quality drop (only for cost-sensitive embed workloads) | embeddings, reranking |

Profile validation steps:
1. Generate baseline outputs (float32) for benchmark prompt set.
2. Generate quantized outputs under identical RNG and input conditions.
3. Compute delta metrics (task metric, embedding drift, token-level latency).
4. Validate against profile acceptance thresholds.

6) Regression triage playbook (runbook)
- Detection:
  - Alert triggers: nightly eval delta > configured threshold, canary smoke failures, customer error reports.
  - Channel: PagerDuty for high-severity (customer-facing regressions), Slack #applied-ml for low/medium.
- Initial triage (first 30 minutes):
  1. Acknowledge alert and assign owner (oncall ML engineer).
  2. Collect artifacts: eval harness outputs, model variant metadata, recent deploy diff, and telemetry samples.
  3. Run quick reproducibility check: rerun failing prompt set locally with same seed.
- Classification and actions:
  - Class A (functional regression, high impact): rollback model route to previous stable revision immediately.
  - Class B (performance regression, latency/cost): scale capacity or revert quantization profile; schedule deeper perf investigation.
  - Class C (minor metric drift): schedule root-cause analysis (RCA) within 5 business days; maintain extra monitoring.
- Post-incident:
  - Produce short postmortem (owner within 3 business days) with: timeline, root cause, corrective actions, and preventive measures.
  - Update prompt sets or quantization profiles as needed; re-run full evals for affected artifacts.

Regression triage checklist:
- [ ] Owner assigned
- [ ] Reproducibility confirmed (Y/N)
- [ ] Classification assigned (A/B/C)
- [ ] Immediate mitigations applied (rollback/scaling)
- [ ] RCA completed and published

7) Metrics and SLOs (recommended defaults)
- Quality SLOs:
  - Task metric SLO: maintain >= 98% of baseline metric for critical tasks (e.g., NER/classification).
  - Embedding drift SLO: mean cosine similarity within 0.03 of baseline.
- Reliability SLOs (per-route):
  - Availability: 99.95%
  - Latency: P95 token-latency < 300ms for small models, < 700ms for medium models on dedicated pools.

8) Related operational notes
- Canary rollout policy:
  - Start at 5% traffic for 24h, increase to 25% for 24h, then 100% if no alerts.
  - Tighten canary for models touching sensitive domains (finance/healthcare): start at 1% and extend windows.
- Artifact retention:
  - Store eval artifacts for 180 days by default; extend to 365 days for enterprise/private customers.

9) Appendix: Useful commands and examples
- Run nightly eval locally (example):
```
ri-eval-run --model $MODEL --prompt-set nightly_core --out artifacts/$MODEL-nightly --runs 1000 --seed 7 --hardware gpu-a100
```
- Compare outputs (quick diff):
```
ri-eval-compare --baseline artifacts/redwood/open-7b:v1/nightly.json --target artifacts/redwood/open-7b:v2/nightly.json --report reports/diff-2028-11-15.html
```
